title: Currency Swaps, Valuation, Legal Risk, and CDS
targetAudiencePersona: Global Macro Risk Manager & Multi-Currency Treasury Trader
prerequisites: Plain vanilla interest rate swap mechanics and comparative advantage from Chapter 7 Part 1
Interest rate parity and forward exchange rates from Chapter 5
Bond pricing and OIS discounting from Chapter 4
learningOutcomes: Differentiate currency swaps from interest rate swaps by modeling initial and terminal principal exchanges.
Execute synthetic foreign currency liability transformations using domestic borrowing advantages.
Calculate comparative advantage arbitrage surpluses arising from international market home biases.
Value currency swaps using bond portfolio decomposition and forward FX contract replication.
Analyze the Hammersmith & Fulham municipal scandal (Snapshot 7.2) and mitigate ultra vires legal risk.
Formulate Credit Default Swap (CDS) mechanics and calculate default protection payoffs: Payoff = (1 - R) * L.

sections.title: Fixed-for-Fixed Currency Swap Architecture
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate currency swap mechanics and contrast with interest rate swaps via principal exchange.
keyPoints: Principal amounts in two currencies are exchanged at inception at spot exchange rate S_0.
Periodic interest payments are exchanged in their respective currencies.
Principal amounts are re-exchanged at maturity at the exact same initial spot rate.
sections.formulaUsed: Inception: L_USD <-> L_GBP; Maturity: L_GBP <-> L_USD

sections.title: Liability Transformation & Comparative Advantage
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Demonstrate cross-border liability synthetic transformation and compute 30 bps arbitrage surplus.
keyPoints: Firms borrow in their domestic home markets where credit spreads are tightest.
US Firm A (USD 5.0% / GBP 7.0%) vs UK Firm B (USD 5.8% / GBP 6.5%).
Total arbitrage surplus equals 80 bps - 50 bps = 30 bps, shared among counterparties.
sections.formulaUsed: Total Surplus = Delta USD Spread - Delta GBP Spread

sections.title: Currency Swap Valuation: Bond Portfolios & Forward FX
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Deconstruct currency swap valuation via bond decomposition V_swap = B_B - S_0 * B_A and forward FX.
keyPoints: Swap is valued as long domestic bond minus spot-converted foreign bond: V_swap = B_B - S_0 * B_A.
Alternatively priced as a portfolio of forward FX contracts using interest rate parity.
Principal exchange at maturity creates significant duration and FX translation sensitivity.

sections.title: Credit Risk Asymmetry & The Hammersmith Scandal
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Analyze credit risk of terminal principal exchange and dissect Snapshot 7.2 legal capacity crisis.
keyPoints: Currency swaps possess far greater credit risk than interest rate swaps due to terminal principal re-exchange.
Hammersmith and Fulham council entered 600 speculative swaps, losing £600M when rates soared to 15%.
UK House of Lords declared contracts ultra vires (void), leaving international banks with £1B losses.
sections.formulaUsed: Credit Exposure = max(0, B_B - S_0 * B_A)

sections.title: Credit Default Swaps (CDS) & Default Payoff Mechanics
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Introduce CDS mechanics, premium spreads, and recovery rate default payoffs.
keyPoints: Protection buyer pays periodic spread (e.g. 150 bps) to insure against reference entity default.
Upon credit event, protection seller pays Payoff = (1 - R) * Notional.
Assuming standard 40% bond recovery rate (R=0.40), default payout equals 60% of notional principal.

misconceptions.misconception: Currency swaps, like interest rate swaps, never exchange principal amounts.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Currency swaps must exchange principal at inception and re-exchange at maturity so counterparties obtain foreign currency capital.

misconceptions.misconception: A legally executed derivative contract with a government body or municipality is always legally binding and enforceable.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The Hammersmith and Fulham scandal proved that if an entity lacks statutory capacity (ultra vires), courts can void contracts entirely with zero compensation.

misconceptions.misconception: A Credit Default Swap pays the full 100% face value of the reference bond upon default.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: CDS contracts pay the loss given default: (1 - R) * Notional, subtracting the recovery rate R realized on defaulted debt.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: An asset manager purchases $20M credit protection on corporate debt via a Credit Default Swap. A credit event occurs, and the defaulted bonds settle in auction with a 40% recovery rate (R = 0.40).
activeRecallQuiz.question: What is the net default insurance payoff received by the protection buyer?
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: The default payoff formula is Payoff = (1 - R) * L = (1 - 0.40) * $20,000,000 = 0.60 * $20M = $12,000,000.

coreTakeaways: Currency swaps exchange principal at inception and maturity, unlike interest rate swaps.
Home market borrowing advantages create comparative advantage surpluses shared internationally.
Currency swaps are valued via bond decomposition: V_swap = B_B - S_0 * B_A.
Terminal principal exchange substantially magnifies credit risk compared to interest rate swaps.
Snapshot 7.2 illustrates ultra vires legal capacity risk that can void valid contracts completely.
Credit Default Swaps transfer default risk, paying (1 - R) * Notional upon a credit event.
